rationale: The unit needs a readable, critical synthesis that supports a guideline and a teaching day, covering effects, harms and programme delivery across trials, observational and experience studies. A narrative review with a documented librarian-supported search, reported against SANRA, fits that purpose and the 40 approved hours. A new systematic review with meta-analysis would largely repeat the 2023 review (c2) and could not resolve the family-written question from three studies; the harms (c3) and uptake findings (c4) are better handled in narrative form. The best effect estimate (c1) is presented with its limits.
alternatives: Systematic review with meta-analysis (refused: a 2023 review exists, only three family-written diary studies could be pooled, and 40 hours is not enough)
Scoping review of diary programme models (refused: the unit's questions include effects and harms, not only mapping)
Adopt the regional consensus statement without a review (refused: it makes no recommendation on who writes the diary)
whyNotMoreComplex: A systematic review with pooling would add precision that the evidence cannot support and would take several times the approved hours; the guideline needs a clear account of what is known and how certain it is, which a structured narrative review provides.

decision.statement: Write a narrative review of family-led intensive care diaries and post-intensive care syndrome, based on a documented librarian-supported search and reported against SANRA, covering effects in patients and relatives, harms of reading, and programme delivery, and stating the low certainty of the effect evidence.
decision.question: Should the ICU produce a narrative review of family-led diaries to support its guideline and teaching day?

criteria.text: The effect evidence is small and fragile, so a synthesis that states its certainty is useful to the unit.
A current review already answers the unit's questions on family-written diaries, harms and delivery.

gates.evidence: Education committee minute EDC-2026-07 approving 40 hours between October 2026 and February 2027, supplied by the investigator
Library request LIB-2026-219 confirmed for October 2026, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Adopt the regional consensus statement without a review
Scoping review of diary programme models
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4, each from a retrieved record, and on the investigator's approval records for both gates.

summary: Narrative review recommended; the decision rests on four ledger claims from retrieved records and both gates are met on investigator-supplied records.
